Kimi K3.1 Pro and K3.1 Pro Highspeed

Kimi K3.1 Pro and K3.1 Pro Highspeed

AI 作者 Jowsey 热度 1067 回复 663 2026/10/24 00:59
打开原帖 打开外部链接 JSON

摘要

  • Introducing Kimi K3.1 ProWe're introducing Kimi K3.1 Pro, the first model in our new K3.1 series and our most capable 3T-class open-weight model to date, with a 1-million-token context window. It delivers substantial improvements across coding, 3D creation, financial research, and other agentic capabilities. We are also releasing Kimi K3.1 Pro Highspeed, which delivers 2-3× the speed of K3.1 Pro for more responsive interactions. Kimi K3.1 Pro and Kimi K3.1 Pro Highspeed are available today on Kimi.ai, Kimi Work, Kimi Code, and the Kimi API. The full model weights will be released by Nov 4.
  • Advancing the Frontier of Open Intelligence Kimi K3.1 Pro is a post-trained version of Kimi K3, with substantially larger post-training compute. To enable large-scale joint RL across hundreds of downstream domains, we optimized every layer of the stack — the RL framework, long-context inference, training efficiency, sandbox infrastructure, rollout scheduling, and a shared platform for environment quality checks — so that each increment of RL compute delivers stable, predictable returns. As a result, K3.1 Pro achieves consistent gains in every domain. Across coding, agentic, and knowledge benchmarks, K3.1 Pro matches or approaches the strongest proprietary models. On Terminal-Bench 4.0, which evaluates coding agents on realistic, resource-constrained terminal tasks using strict task-specific tests, K3.1 Pro scores 65.7%, ahead of GPT-6 Astra (58.2%) and narrowly behind Claude Opus 5.5 (66.4%). And on Kimi Code Bench 3.0 Long-horizon, our internal benchmark that tests coding agents' multi-step execution, tool use, and end-to-end problem solving across diverse engineering domains, K3.1 Pro scores 61.2%, above K3's 55.95%.

lxe 2026/10/25 02:58
That's because every single model release after GPT-3.5 has been, at least in part, been trained on data synthesized by GPT-3.5 and then the other OpenAI models, as well as Anthropic models later.

Also the distillation attacks and other distillation methods that gather chain of thought information from frontier models are also used to generate vast amounts of data in order to generate synthetic datasets to post-train what I believe is the vast majority of models that are being released.

If you look at any information about how these models are trained, the details about how the data has been synthesized, where the agentic traces come from that are used in post-training, etc., they almost never tell you about exactly what model was used to generate them.
